tier_reason: README compares against llama.cpp Q2_K/Q4_0 kernels with the quoted 20/48 tok/s and '4~5x' figures; the same comparison is published in the peer-reviewed EuroSys 2025 paper (arXiv 2407.00088), which claims up to 4x throughput over llama.cpp. Benchmark script (tools/bench_e2e.py) is public but per-run compiler flags are not stated, so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Clang 17.0.6 is the documented build toolchain (Windows install notes); llama.cpp built with -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DLLAMA_TMAC=ON; exact flags for the published runs not stated
corrections.hardware: Surface Laptop 7, Apple M2-Ultra, Jetson AGX Orin, Raspberry Pi 5, Surface Book 3
corrections.caveats: Numbers are from the authors (README and EuroSys'25 paper, arXiv 2407.00088; paper abstract says 'up to 4x' vs llama.cpp, README says 4~5x) against llama.cpp b2794 (May 2024). README notes llama.cpp throughput was unstable under thermal limits in 'Better Performance' mode, so a 'Best Performance' re-profile was added; authors warn old x86 platforms may see little speedup, especially for 4-bit. Baseline not in the category list.

notes: Upgraded C->B on the peer-reviewed EuroSys 2025 paper (authors are the project team, so it is peer-reviewed but not independent). Metadata (MIT, last commit 2025-06-03, stale) checked and correct.
